scope: Optional finite operator-action and reduced-state teaching bridges, lazy lesson integration, and guarded example/file loading.
verification: The finite Fock convention, 128 actions and eight cross-sector maps are checked against independent Jordan-Wigner operators and the production Python models.

Complex phase probes distinguish coherent addition from random local measurements, use conjugate creation coefficients, and include dark transition candidates. Explicit input copying waits for a manual full-tool calculation.
Reduced-state checks include a genuinely complex off-diagonal rhoB, mixed-state counterexamples, Schmidt probabilities and units, triplet projection, and independent finite periodic AKLT states.
Real course integration preserves native open state, local controls and unsubmitted choices while retaining original incomplete lab drafts, course exercises and scientific records.
The optional mathematical modules are requested only by exact learning hooks; retries, detached views and stale callbacks are isolated.
Pending file/example reads prevent immediate Run and Enter submission; explicit retry, input replacement and calculation-finally races are exercised.
limitations: These are bounded teaching references, not additional general scientific solvers or evidence for measured learning outcomes.

The Hubbard spectral example fixes two sites, a unique noninteracting pure ground state and a normalized probe. General interacting and degenerate-state computations remain in the original Python tools.
Local subsystem entropy quantifies entanglement only for an overall pure state; mixed global states with the same local density matrix are distinguished.
A periodic-chain cut can cross multiple virtual bonds. Its finite Schmidt rank is not identified with a single virtual bond dimension.
Only seven reviewed lessons have the new panels; the broad curriculum and complete tool-workflow audit remain open.
